goal: Work on a machine that is somewhere else
why: A person opens a desktop, a single program or a shell of a machine that is somewhere else, in a browser, and works there as if sitting at it.
A person signs in once, where the organisation already signs in, and is then signed in on the machine too, from any device.
Two people look at the same session from wherever each is: one shows, helps or takes over.
To open a machine, Away has to know it: what it is, where it is, how it is reached and signed in to, whether it is on.
An organisation is many people and many machines: each person sees and reaches only what they may, and does there only what they may.
Whoever answers for the machines can say afterwards who was on which one, when, as whom, and what was done there.
Somebody runs it: installs it, makes it reachable, keeps it up to date, and learns when it fails.
It opens the door to every machine it knows, so anyone can see what it does, check it, change it, and count on it staying open.
